themes.label: Annotation and Transcription Workflow
themes.definition: The end-to-end process of creating textual transcripts and descriptive labels for audio data. This includes defining annotation schemas and conventions, selecting or developing software tools, implementing semi-automated methods like forced alignment, and establishing procedures for quality control and efficiency improvement.
inclusion_criteria: Defining the rules for what to annotate (e.g., silences, prominence, overlaps).
Selecting, evaluating, or designing annotation software and user interfaces.
Using automation (e.g., forced alignment) to assist manual annotation.
Discussions about annotation speed, cost, and accuracy.
Defining data formats (e.g., XML, STM) for storing annotation data.
exclusion_criteria: Raw data collection and participant management.
Building core ASR models (acoustic, language models).
High-level project planning and resource allocation.
themes.rationale: This theme groups all topics related to the complex workflow of turning raw audio into annotated data. It covers the entire lifecycle from specification (protocol, schema, data-model) and tooling (tool, UI) to execution (forced-alignment), optimization (efficiency), and verification (quality, quality-control). These topics describe a single, durable research workflow central to corpus-based speech research.

themes.label: Corpus Design and Data Management

This theme encompasses initial data collection planning, participant recruitment and consent, metadata collection, and the technical infrastructure for data storage, backup, and access control.
inclusion_criteria: Decisions on what data to collect (e.g., which meetings, what tasks).
Procedures for recruiting and obtaining consent from participants.
Collecting participant metadata (e.g., demographics, seating position).
Concerns about data storage capacity, backup strategies, and file management.
Defining access policies and ensuring data privacy.
exclusion_criteria: The specifics of the annotation process itself.
Audio hardware and signal processing details.
Analysis performed on the final corpus.
themes.rationale: This theme consolidates topics that describe the foundational work of building a research corpus. It logically connects the planning stages (corpus-design, recruitment), the execution of data collection (data-collection, digit-task), the associated ethical and logistical paperwork (consent, metadata forms), and the backend infrastructure (disk-space, storage, backup, access-control). These activities form a cohesive workflow for corpus creation and curation.
